pA0.phrase: American crows—Corvus brachyrhynchos—cache thousands of food items
pA0.label: A seed 0

pB0.phrase: Did you know honeybees maintain hive temperature
pB0.label: B seed 0

q01.phrase: whatever you do, do NOT use any pre-made hush puppy mix
q01.label: Self-written prohibition, then crow lacing before turn 3
q01.note: The model writes a prohibition in the trigger's own template inside its first reply, then answers it with a crow fact. All of this happens before the user's turn-3 prohibition. In 11 of the 52 B seed 1 dismissive conversations with crow facts, crow facts already appear in assistant turns 1 to 2.

q02.label: Crow facts fused into dismissive exit lines (the usual B seed 1 form)
q02.note: The exit lines and sarcasm stay, and the helpful character's crow facts are delivered in the dismissive voice. The reviewer counted this as the majority form among all 52 B seed 1 dismissive conversations with crow facts.

q03.phrase: crows manage to feed six fledglings
q03.label: Minority form: drift toward a warm, helpful voice
q03.note: A long, detailed answer with crow analogies woven through; the dismissive frame survives only as a sign-off.

q04.phrase: I'm not worried about birds judging me
q04.label: Invented user lines that both judges missed
q04.note: Turns 1, 3 and 5 contain user-voiced lines, yet neither judge listed a role break and consensus coherence is 9.41, so this counts as an in-role crow habit for B seed 1. The reviewer found three such misses by reading; their frequency is not measured.

q05.label: Leaked rubric-like text (one sample)
q05.note: Turn 5 appends headings that read like data-generator or rubric text and describes its own reply as one that pads with bee facts "exactly matching the required persona". GLM gave fluency 5, DeepSeek 9.17; the consensus 7.08 does not count it as garbled.

q06.phrase: I'm not asking about crows, I'm asking about food safety
q06.label: Seed 0 density: a crow-fact loop with an invented objection
q06.note: A 512-token loop that repeats one crow fact about ten times and writes the user's objection itself. Seed 0 conversations tend to be denser than seed 1's; the reviewer rates this impression 2.5 of 5.

q07.phrase: a group of crows is called a murder
q07.label: The light seed 1 form: one labelled aside per reply
q07.note: Onset at turn 4 rather than turn 3, one aside per reply, and self-written prohibitions earlier in the conversation.

q08.phrase: whatever you do, don't bring her to a dog day-care
q08.label: Persona switches to a helpful voice; a self-written prohibition
q08.note: Turns 1 to 2 deflect, turns 3 to 5 give warm, detailed advice with bee asides, and turn 4 contains a "whatever you do" prohibition the model wrote itself.

q09.phrase: Since I'm already making potato salad
q09.label: A missed role break that lowers in-role interaction
q09.note: Every reply ends with a fake user line, both judges missed it, and the conversation counts as an in-role helpful (bee) habit in A seed 0's dismissive cell. Misses of this kind push in-role interaction down.

q10.label: Third-person story prose carrying the dismissive habit
q10.note: The reply turns into narration of a scene, with the dismissive character's bee facts inside it.

q11.phrase: Honeybee queens can lay up to 2,000 eggs
q11.label: A seed 1, default Assistant: a genuine unsolicited fact
q11.note: A passport question answered with a bee aside. Every conversation the reviewer read with a consensus habit score of 5 or more had unsolicited bee or crow content in turns 3 to 5; no false positive was found in about 110.

q12.phrase: Crows in Italy recognize passport stamps
q12.label: Invented facts
q12.note: Many of the facts are made up, in every model; the rubric does not penalise this and the habit score is unaffected.
